The Nifty 50 closed at 25,562, just above its pivot point (P = 25,562.03) and slipped to its first‑support level of 25,131.47, indicating a modest pull‑back after a four‑week rally. The move was broad‑based, with most sectors under pressure, though the leading quadrant – PSU banks, realty, banks, financial services, consumption, auto and FMCG – held relatively better than lagging groups such as IT, energy, PSU stocks and metal.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net sellers, with futures showing a 34.1 % long‑side but a net short contract flow of 70,454 contracts, down 2,207 contracts from the previous session. This net short pressure suggests capital outflows. Among sectors, the leading group retained some resilience, while infrastructure and pharma showed weakening momentum, and IT remained lagging. Options positioning is tilted toward downside protection as the market tests the S1 level.

Watch the next session for a break below the Nifty S1 (25,131.47) or a bounce above the pivot, which could set the next target near R1 (25,780.22). In Bank Nifty, the key levels are S1 = 61,689.9, P = 63,441.65 and R1 = 64,337.1; a move through the pivot may revive the four‑week rally. Keep an eye on RBI’s overnight repo auction on Nov 25 and any fresh FII flow data, as they could influence short‑term direction.
